newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BLACKBURN WILL PART WITH ERIKSSON - FOR A PRICE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLACKBURN WILL PART WITH ERIKSSON - FOR A PRICE.

text.p: Blackburn have asked Lazio for 500,000 pounds ($800,000) for Swedish coach Sven-Goran Eriksson, who has committed himself to joining the English premier league club at the end of the season, an Italian newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Corriere dello Sport said Blackburn made the offer to the Roman club some 10 days ago.
The daily said Lazio had denied receiving the offer. No-one at the club was immediately available for comment.

Eriksson, who has managed Sampdoria for five years after spells with Roma and Fiorentina, signed an agreement in December to take over at Blackburn when his contract with Sampdoria expires at the end of the season.
But after hoisting Sampdoria to second place in the league table, Eriksson has appeared reluctant to leave Italy and media reports have linked him to Lazio, among other clubs.

Lazio are seeking a manager for next season after sacking Czech coach Zdenek Zeman and temporarily replacing him with club president Dino Zoff, captain and goalkeeper of Italy's 1982 World Cup-winning side.
Eriksson, who spent five successful seasons with Portugal's Benfica before moving to Italy, told reporters in Genoa on Wednesday that he would make an announcement on his future in the coming weeks.

He added that his career goal was to win a European trophy but confirmed that, even if Sampdoria finished second in the league and gained a place in next season's European Cup, he would still leave the club.

"For us to win the title we would need one of the biggest surprises for 15 years but whatever happens I will be leaving Sampdoria," said Eriksson, who lost a European Cup final and a UEFA Cup final with Benfica.
"Three or four months ago nobody believed we could finish even second and if we get into Europe it would be regarded as a great achievement."
